copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. South Africa v Korea Republic in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Thursday, and the model and the market disagree on the Korea Republic side by +16.1pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Korea Republic 150 points higher than the other side (South Africa 1620, Korea Republic 1770). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: South Africa to win at 23%, the draw at 21%, and Korea Republic to win at 56%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Korea Republic sits at 56% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: South Africa to win at 30%, the draw at 29%, and Korea Republic to win at 40%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Korea Republic side — 40% on the market, 56% on the engine, a +16.1pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 47% — +7.7pp clear of the market's 40%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Korea Republic priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 33 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Korea Republic side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Korea Republic look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 56% vs market 40% — a +16.1pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: South Africa v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
